agree.reason: The plain apology and the new field will help, but this reader's real grievance was silence and no credit during bad weeks, and the email doesn't promise weekly updates or credit for weather-cut boxes, so they have little reason to think a bad week would go differently next time.

honest.reason: The figures match the brief, but 'reply and I'll hold a share' invents a sign-up process when signup actually runs through the website, and 'crops people count on most' claims more than the facts support.

works_the_facts.reason: Turning six half-full weeks into 'roughly three weeks of vegetables you paid for' is a strong derivation, but the email never puts a dollar figure on it (about $74) and doesn't show how scarce the 52 remaining shares are.

right_comparison.reason: It never shows the reader what a bad week would look like under the new arrangement compared with last July, so the reader has no picture of what is different.

qualification.reason: 'No farm can control the weather' is a vague hedge with no checkable commitment attached, when the email could have promised credit for any week weather cuts a box by more than a third.

objections.reason: The objection that 'you went quiet and gave nothing back' gets an apology but no fix, because the pause credit covers missed pickups, not weather losses, and the email offers no promise of regular updates.

fit.reason: It is an email under 200 words with a clear subject line, but it's unsigned with no farm name and no sign-up link.
